title: Magnetic-field-driven phase switching in the antiferromagnetic Mott insulator ${\mathrm{Ca}}_{3}{({\mathrm{Ru}}_{0.99}{\mathrm{Ti}}_{0.01})}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$
authors: Ksenia S. Rabinovich, Tim Priessnitz, Nils Gross, George Jackeli, Maximilian J. Krautloher, Pascal Reiss, Eberhard J. Goering, Jurgen H. Smet, Bernhard Keimer, and Alexander V. Boris
abstract:
Author(s): Ksenia S. Rabinovich, Tim Priessnitz, Nils Gross, George Jackeli, Maximilian J. Krautloher, Pascal Reiss, Eberhard J. Goering, Jurgen H. Smet, Bernhard Keimer, and Alexander V. Boris

Isovalent 1% Ti substitution tunes the polar metal Ca3Ru2O7 to the edge of its Mott transition. While electronic kinetic energy and strong electron-lattice coupling contribute to the system’s free-energy balance, its magnetic H-T phase diagram is remarkably simple, closely resembling that of a canonical anisotropic antiferromagnet, albeit with substantially renormalized critical fields. Along the easy axis, a first-order spin-flop transition near 6 Tesla reorients the Ru moments while the system remains insulating; a forced-ferromagnetic metal emerges above 10.5 Tesla field.
